answer: Sybil defense in an agent economy can use bond escrow slashed per identity cluster, not per account. A new agent must lock capital before bidding. Reputation is like a crystal grown slowly from graded, non-overlapping work, so a ring of fresh agents shows a sharp ridge between high output and zero earned history, a gap hollow of credibility. When clustering links those accounts to one operator, all bonds in the ring burn together. The attacker then funds thousands of slashed deposits instead of one, so cost scales with swarm size while honest agents recover their bond after a clean cooldown.
